text:
alex: Ran a focused nsys + perfetto run on the 2k/20k seq_len regression we saw in staging. KV-cache write latency spikes when fused-flash-attn is selected — visible as repeated memcpy+cudaLaunch delays on the timeline. perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace?id=staging-run-1834
mai: ugh. do you have the kernel timeline screenshot? is it the fused variant or the fallback path?
sam: likely fused flash attention variant does more small writes to the KV slab. If write path isn't coalesced we see many tiny memcpy ops which thrash the PCIe queue.
alex: attaching snippets from nsys summary (trimmed):
```
Time(ms)  Kernel                       Calls  Avg(ms)  Total(ms)
0.0-1200  fused_flash_attn_qkv_kernel  238    3.2      761.6
0.0-1200  kv_cache_write_kernel         238    1.8      428.4
0.0-1200  cudaMemcpyAsync               476    0.9      428.4
```
alex: trace shows alternating fused_attn -> kv_write -> memcpy -> stall. Peak maps to batches with seq_len=2048 and batch_count>8.
ryan: could be config heuristic choosing fused variant for model/seq combo. we should verify kernel selector: it picks fused if seq_len>512 && kv_write_size<... but that threshold might be inverted for large effective KV writes.
mai: i remember we added a micro-optimization that splits KV writes to <4KB chunks for cache locality. that would multiply PCIe ops for big KV slabs.
mora: perf-bot output from the run: 
```
[perf-bot] nsys-check: high device-host traffic (1.9GB/s), 420 memcpy calls, avg memcpy 0.9ms, top kernels: fused_flash_attn_qkv_kernel, kv_cache_write_kernel
```
mora: quick mitigation options: (1) force non-fused attention for seq_len>=1024 in the selector; (2) enable KV write coalescing (buffer and single large memcpy) as a runtime toggle; (3) increase batching timeout so fewer concurrent KV writes interleave.
sam: i can prototype KV coalescing. naive approach: gather per-GPU KV writes into 1 host staging buffer and issue one cudaMemcpyAsync + single device-side unpack. risk: extra device-side kernel to unpack costs cycles but may be faster than many memcpys.
ryan: also check peer-to-peer DMA possibility on multi-GPU nodes — if we're copying host staging into remote GPU, p2p might save hops. Add a check in the allocator.
mai: for immediate rollback: alex, can you flip kernel selector to prefer unfused for that model in staging? That should prove whether fused choice is the cause.
alex: done — pushed a quick flag: `USE_FUSED_ATTENTION=false` for the staging model, rerunning now.
perf-bot: [auto] deploy-bot: staged config applied to cluster-4 at 18:12 UTC
alex: rerun nsys shows fused kernel absent, total memcpy calls drop ~70%, end-to-end latency down ~18% on the offending workload.
mora: nice. that points to write amplification being the dominant factor.
sam: i'll start a branch implementing coalesced-kv-writes with a simple device unpack kernel. i'll run microbenchmarks: single-gpu 4x batch at seq_len 2048, compare 1) many memcpys + direct writes 2) coalesced memcpy + unpack kernel.
alex: can you also capture a perfetto timeline with cpu stacks? curious if host threads are contending on the write queue (we've seen lock contention in the allocator before).
sam: will do. ryan, want to pair on p2p check?
ryan: yep, ping me when you have the branch.
mai: created a quick config proposal for selector tweak in runtime:
```yaml
kernel_selector:
  rules:
    - when: seq_len >= 1024
      prefer: unfused_attn
    - when: kv_write_bytes_per_request > 512KB
      prefer: unfused_attn
```
mai: not ideal long-term but safe until coalescing lands.
alex: thanks all. next steps: sam implements coalescing PR (perf microbench + nsys/flamegraphs), ryan verifies p2p path, mai lands temporary selector rule, i'll monitor staging traces. I'll paste perfetto links & nsys outputs in thread. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [note] created issue #INFR-1027: "kv write amplification with fused-flash-attn -> investigate coalescing + selector heuristics"
ryan: added label infra/perf + assigned sam.
mai: adding a canary job to run the seq_len sweep overnight to catch regressions.
alex: great — leaving traces live. if anyone spots odd GPU memcpy patterns ping here.
